Hi Sandra,

Really appreciate the level of detail — totally reasonable asks. High level options we typically propose for pilots to address auditor requirements:

1) Remote-limited operator (no exec, monitoring-only): Redwood operators have monitoring and read-only metrics access. Evidence: access logs + role-based session logs.
2) Split-ops handover (preferred for customers who want control): deliver encrypted snapshot of model runtime and KV state to customer-controlled storage together with an attestation letter. Operator credentials provided only to named admins for a limited handover window; keys rotated afterwards. Evidence: signed snapshot hash, rotation confirmation, operator access audit trail.
3) Full customer-controlled operator (on-prem handoff): Redwood performs initial install support, then we hand over operator credentials to customer SOC; Redwood commits to a support SLA but not continuous access. Evidence: delivery confirmation + runbook and support tickets.

I think option 2 maps to what you're describing. I'll loop in Legal to get concrete redline language for the MSA/addendum and a narrow set of commitments for the Order Form. Proposed timeline: we prepare a redline draft by EOD Thu and a short summary page for your auditors.

Quick ask for your procurement team: do you require an escrow-style custody transfer (third-party escrow) or is the encrypted snapshot + attestation sufficient?

Jonas — good summary. Quick legal guidance below; I've kept the options and added specific limited-language you can propose to the customer.

1) License scope language (MSA addendum bullet):
  - "During the Pilot, Redwood will retain title to the Model and grants the Customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to operate the Model within Customer-controlled infrastructure strictly for evaluation purposes. Operator capabilities are limited to those expressly enumerated in the Order Form (monitoring, health checks, incident remediation) and exclude any capability to exfiltrate training data or to run arbitrary code against customer datasets without explicit prior written consent."

2) Evidence delivery (Order Form annex):
  - "Evidence Package: For the purposes of customer audits, Redwood will deliver an Evidence Package consisting of: (i) a cryptographically signed snapshot (sha256 hash) of the runtime image and configuration; (ii) operator access logs covering the period requested; and (iii) a signed Attestation Letter confirming key rotation following snapshot delivery. Delivery will be to a Customer‑controlled secure storage endpoint (e.g., S3) or to a mutually agreed third party archive. Redwood's obligation is limited to delivery and attestation; Redwood is not responsible for Customer's archival or custodial controls post-delivery."

3) Narrowing custody/escrow exposure:
  - Avoid language that transfers custody beyond delivery and attestation. If Customer insists on third-party escrow, treat that as a separate SOW with fees and an explicit escrow agreement.

4) Operational controls and auditability:
  - Require documented, time-bound admin accounts for any handover and mandatory key rotation within 24 hours of handover. Include a support SLA for any handover window.

5) Redlines and approvals:
  - I'm attaching a tracked redline (proposed_addendum_redlines.docx) that implements the above. Laura — please sanity check the indemnity/limitation crossrefs; Aditya — can you confirm the operational feasibility of snapshot + signed hash and the key rotation timeline?

If we can get Ops and Security confirmation, we can send this clean redline to Acme with a short cover memo for their auditors.
